project-charter.title: Observe the Suspension System

cards.title: Client Brief & Study Scope
cards.body: TVS Motor & Hero MotoCorp Suspension Testing Division requires you to perform a system-level engineering analysis of an automobile motorcycle rear suspension system.

cards.title: System-Level Mechanical Interaction
cards.body: An automobile suspension is a complete mechanical system consisting of the motorcycle frame, swingarm, helical spring, hydraulic damper, mounting bushings, rear axle, wheel, and tyre working together to absorb road bumps, maintain tyre grip, and provide ride stability.

cards.title: Engineering Objectives
items: Observe the complete motorcycle rear suspension system on Engineering Asset EA-15.
Identify all major structural, elastic, damping, and pivoting components.
Trace the load transmission path from road impact to motorcycle frame.
Analyze suspension compression and rebound dynamics.
Diagnose practical suspension fault conditions and render system-level tuning decisions.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I have read and understood the EA-15 Project Charter for Automobile Suspension System Analysis.

component-identification.title: Identify Suspension Components
component-identification.description: Student engineering asset illustrating motorcycle rear suspension assembly and structural components.

labels.feedback: Main structural frame carrying engine, rider load, and suspension mounts.
Upper frame eyelet anchoring top of spring-damper unit.
Internal hydraulic damper controlling oscillation velocity.
Coiled elastic spring supporting vehicle weight and storing impact energy.
Bottom eyelet connecting suspension unit to swingarm assembly.
Pivoting shaft allowing swingarm arc motion relative to main frame.
Trailing arm guiding rear wheel up-and-down motion.
Progressive rate linkage connecting swingarm to shock unit.
Transverse axle locating rear wheel hub on swingarm dropouts.
Rotational wheel rim transmitting torque and supporting tyre.
Pneumatic tyre providing friction grip and initial high-frequency bump compliance.

load-transmission-path.title: Understand the Load Transmission Path
load-transmission-path.prompt: Trace how road impact forces travel through the suspension components to the motorcycle frame.

mcq.question: Which sequence correctly describes the load transmission path from road irregularity to rider chassis?

options.label: Road Irregularity → Tyre → Wheel Rim → Rear Axle → Swingarm → Spring & Damper Unit → Upper Mount → Frame Chassis
Frame Chassis → Helical Spring → Tyre → Road Irregularity → Swingarm → Rear Axle
Road Irregularity → Damper → Frame Chassis → Tyre → Wheel Rim → Rear Axle
Swingarm → Rear Axle → Tyre → Wheel Rim → Helical Spring → Frame Chassis

component-functions.title: Identify Component Functions
component-functions.prompt: Evaluate the specific mechanical function performed by each component in the rear suspension assembly.

mcq.question: Which statement correctly describes the primary mechanical function of the swingarm and swingarm pivot?

options.label: The swingarm guides the rear wheel in a controlled arc relative to the frame while transferring driving traction force from tyre to chassis.
The swingarm dissipates high frequency fluid heat generated by the brake disc.
The swingarm stores elastic strain energy to replace the helical spring.
The swingarm locks the rear wheel rigidly to prevent any vertical or angular motion.

spring-and-damper.title: Spring and Damper
spring-and-damper.prompt: Distinguish between the elastic energy storage role of the spring and the kinetic dissipation role of the damper.

mcq.question: Why is a vehicle suspension incapable of functioning satisfactorily with ONLY a helical compression spring and no shock absorber?

options.label: Without a damper, the spring stores bump energy and continues oscillating uncontrollably at its natural frequency, causing severe vehicle instability and rider bouncing.
Without a damper, the spring immediately snaps into two pieces upon first bump impact.
Without a damper, the motorcycle engine cannot transmit rotational torque to the rear wheel.
Without a damper, the tyre pressure drops to zero instantly.

suspension-movement.title: Suspension Movement
suspension-movement.prompt: Analyze the mechanical behavior of the suspension during bump compression and subsequent rebound.

mcq.question: What occurs during the rebound phase after the rear wheel passes over the crest of a road bump?

options.label: The compressed spring extends to push the wheel back down, while the hydraulic damper metering valves resist rapid extension to prevent harsh wheel rebound.
The spring compresses further while the damper locks solid to prevent wheel extension.
The swingarm detaches from the pivot pin until the next bump.
The damper fluid boils and reverses flow into the fuel tank.

suspension-performance.title: Suspension Performance
suspension-performance.prompt: Evaluate the engineering trade-off between ride comfort and vehicle road holding / cornering stability.

mcq.question: How does increasing spring stiffness and damping coefficient affect motorcycle ride characteristics?

options.label: It improves high-speed cornering stability and reduces chassis roll/pitch, but increases harshness felt by the rider over small road ripples.
It makes the suspension feel completely soft like a luxury saloon while increasing body sway.
It eliminates all vertical forces acting on the rear axle housing.
It increases maximum suspension travel by 500%.

components.name: Suspension Bottoms Out Hard Under Passenger Payload
components.label: Bottoming Out Impact Diagnosis

options.title: WORN DAMPER SEALS (BOUNCING) & INSUFFICIENT SPRING PRELOAD / STIFFNESS (BOTTOMING)
options.description: Repeated bouncing indicates loss of damping fluid / worn shock valving; metallic bottoming out indicates inadequate spring preload or spring rate for heavy passenger payload.

options.title: BENT REAR AXLE (BOUNCING) & OVER-INFLATED TYRE (BOTTOMING)
options.description: Rear axle bending causes wheel misalignment rather than oscillation; over-inflated tyre increases ride harshness rather than causing suspension bottoming.

options.title: INCREASE PRELOAD & REBOUND DAMPING FOR DUAL-RIDER; INCREASE TRAVEL & COMPRESSION DAMPING FOR OFF-ROAD
options.description: Dual-rider payload requires increased spring preload and rebound control to prevent sagging; off-road riding requires longer suspension travel and tuned compression damping to absorb high-velocity impacts.

options.title: RETAIN STOCK SOFT CITY COMMUTER SETTINGS FOR ALL CONDITIONS
options.description: Stock soft commuter settings will bottom out severely under heavy touring payload and cause loss of tyre grip on rough off-road terrain.
